newsitem.title: UK: Prism to end founders "share ratchet' system.
newsitem.headline: Prism to end founders "share ratchet' system.

text.p: British passenger train operator Prism Rail Plc said on Monday it had terminated a preferential investment system with its founder investors, who created the company last year to enter Britain's new private rail market.

The arrangement, known as a "share ratchet", was a means of allowing the founders to scale up their stake in the firm's equity as they supported its growth. Prism now has four of the country's 25 regional rail franchises and is bidding for others.
In a statement Prism described the termination of the ratchet as reflecting its bidding success "and the fact that the continuing need for a ratchet mechanism no longer exists".
"In return, Prism will be responsible for any costs and expenses associated with tenders submitted in the current and final round of (franchise) bidding.

"Since part of these costs has already been met and capitalised by the founder investors, they will be entitled to convert a sufficient number of their existing deferred shares into ordinary shares to a value equal to such costs and expenses borne," it added.
The conversion price would be based on a calculation made after the initial selection of a bidder for two upcoming franchises by the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising.
